# Sweep 24 — DEFENCE THAT DOES NOT SLOW THE KILL

**Run 2026-08-11 (started 18:08:03Z, `date -u`).** A NEW row on the wheel, generated by a
doctrine change rather than by the rotation: `PROGRAMME.md` replaced `PLAY_DEFENCE: never`
with **`PLAY_DEFENCE: not_at_the_kill_s_expense`** and
**`DEFENCE_ADMISSION_BAR: kill_round_non_regression`** earlier the same day.

**Four arms.** (A) what a defensive purchase actually bought through a bounded window, and
what it cost in tempo · (B) **did anyone MEASURE that a defensive addition did not slow
their own attack** · (C) where the purchase demonstrably cost the kill, and what the tell
was · (D) investments that serve defence and offence at once.

---

## THE HEADLINE — arm B is a HARD MEASURED NEGATIVE, and it is the most useful thing here

**Nobody in this field has ever run our bar. The vocabulary for it does not appear.**

Corpus: **41 flattened primary documents, 166,155 words** — all 22 official Battlecode
postmortems 2019-2026, the XSquare guide and alext's 2026 postmortem (24 Battlecode
documents), Halite II/III writeups, Screeps docs and forum threads, Terminal (C1 Games)
starter algo and the 3rd-place APAC team's algorithm README, Jay Scott's StarCraft AI
ladder articles.

* **A/B testing is ROUTINE and named** — Just Woke Up *"doing AB tests against our various
  versions of old bots"*, alext, SPAARK's `runmatches.py`.
* **Every reported outcome is a WIN RATE or a RATING.** Not one is a duration.
* **27 duration / time-to-win phrasings → 1 hit in 166,155 words**, and that hit
  (*"in the other it slowed our progress considerably"*, BC2020 The High Ground) is about
  **cows blocking their wall**, not a defensive investment.

Full detail and both near-misses: **[`nobody-in-the-field-has-ever-measured-the-kill-round`](nobody-in-the-field-has-ever-measured-the-kill-round.md)**.

**⇒ THREE CONSEQUENCES FOR THE PROGRAMME, and the second is the one that will bite:**

1. **There is no precedent to port.** No constants, no estimators, no thresholds. Any
   prereg claiming "the field does X for the tempo bar" is inventing it.
2. **A kill-round bar run on our own arena inherits the exact defect that nearly cost the
   BC2025 champion the title.** They A/B-tested their defensive addition against their own
   past bots; it came back *"usually went even in wins, or even slightly lost"*; they
   shipped it anyway on a population argument — *"our bot wasn’t super aggressive"* — and
   credit it with the two wins that won them the tournament. **A defensive plank whose
   purpose is to survive an aggressive opponent cannot be adjudicated against a fixture
   that is not aggressive.** The bar must be read on unrated legs against live teams.
3. **The one near-experiment in the corpus measures only the COST side.** cout for clout
   priced their "sitting duck" defensive assignment by deleting the units from the fight
   (*"a simple test of 47 vs 50 ducks… the version with 47 lost 90% of the games"*), with
   the defensive benefit removed from the experiment entirely.

## WHAT THE OTHER THREE ARMS RETURNED

**(A) The purchase, and its price.** Everyone who bought a window bought it with something
they already had, and the price is always denominated in **actions foregone**, never in
resources.

* **The canonical statement predates our amendment by nine years and is its POSITIVE
  form** — Jay Scott: *"static defense has to pay for itself with a countervailing
  advantage"*, and the overshoot priced as a dose: *"5 sunkens are 4 too many"*.
  → [`static-defence-must-name-what-the-safety-bought`](static-defence-must-name-what-the-safety-bought.md)
* **The champion's anti-rush bought NO structure — it reordered a queue it already had**,
  and named the tempo cost in the same sentence (*"could sometimes set us back in terms of
  building other towers"*).
  → [`reprioritise-the-existing-queue-instead-of-buying-a-defender`](reprioritise-the-existing-queue-instead-of-buying-a-defender.md)
* **Every window purchase in the field terminates on an EVENT, not a round number.** Five
  cases, four leagues. The single round number in the set is confused's `round < 250`, and
  it is an **OR-clause backstop** on an event-driven state.
  → [`the-window-purchase-terminates-on-an-event-not-a-round-number`](the-window-purchase-terminates-on-an-event-not-a-round-number.md)

**(C) Where it cost the kill — and the tell was always an OPPONENT, never a statistic.**

* **BC2019 smite's "Emergency Defense" is the completest self-diagnosis in the corpus**:
  *"This code allowed us to survive early in the game but had a major unintended
  consequence"*, then three named costs — bad trades, *"stalling global production"*, and
  *"using so much fuel to be produced that they could no longer attack"*. **They caught it
  during the season because ONE opponent farmed it**, and their response was to add a
  scout, not more defence.
  → [`the-defensive-reflex-that-outlived-its-window`](the-defensive-reflex-that-outlived-its-window.md)
* **BC2023 don't @ me DELETED the recall**, and the stated reason is time:
  *"falling back to defend HQs wasted far too much time, and rarely if ever gave us a
  competitive advantage"* — the only sentence in the corpus reporting both sides of a
  defensive trade at once, though with no number on either.
  → [`the-recall-to-defend-was-deleted-for-costing-time`](the-recall-to-defend-was-deleted-for-costing-time.md)

**(D) Dual purpose — the structural answer is TIME, not placement.**

* **Terminal's Lostkids multiplex one wall between seal and gate** on two live booleans
  (*"whether the algorithm is attacking and whether the enemy is attacking"*) and publish
  the exact vulnerability it opens: *"Our defense opens up the side when we are attacking"*.
  Nobody else in the corpus names the cost of dual-purposing at all.
  → [`the-dual-role-structure-is-time-multiplexed-and-it-names-its-cost`](the-dual-role-structure-is-time-multiplexed-and-it-names-its-cost.md)
* **The same team picks the FORM of defence on a predicted dose** — consumable
  (interceptor) against a repeated stream, permanent (wall) against one big pulse. The only
  rule in the corpus that chooses *which kind* rather than *how much*.
  → [`the-consumable-blocker-versus-the-permanent-one`](the-consumable-blocker-versus-the-permanent-one.md)
* **A NEGATIVE that closes a road: BC2025's defensive structure earns income for
  defending** (*"generates chips upon attacking enemy units"*) — dual-purpose by designer
  fiat. **Even so the top-tier equilibrium was two of them, gated, or none.** Our turrets
  produce nothing, consume the currency that funds the kill, and add +20% to the global
  scale. **"The winners used defensive structures, so we should" imports a unit that paid
  for itself onto one that cannot.**
  → [`the-defender-that-pays-income-is-an-affordance-we-do-not-have`](the-defender-that-pays-income-is-an-affordance-we-do-not-have.md)
* **A cheap rebuild SUBSTITUTES for defence.** BC2025's runner-up disabled his defensive
  structures because a destroy-rebuild loop made losing one nearly free: *"defense towers
  were no longer necessary to my strategy since I wanted to destroy my own towers, so I
  disabled them"*.
  → [`a-cheap-rebuild-loop-substitutes-for-defence`](a-cheap-rebuild-loop-substitutes-for-defence.md)

**AND THE COUNTERWEIGHT, filed deliberately.** The strongest published argument that
defence simply wins is the Screeps **mirror argument** — *"you can just employ the mirror
strategy - whatever the other guy does you do the same. You have towers, so you win with
equal code."* Our game satisfies its premises (symmetric maps, identical entity lists,
team-keyed scale). **It names its own two exceptions and both are exactly our programme:
choosing when the fight happens, and attacks aimed at bugs in the defence code.**
→ [`the-mirror-argument-and-the-one-thing-it-cannot-mirror`](the-mirror-argument-and-the-one-thing-it-cannot-mirror.md)

## THE SINGLE MOST BUILDABLE ITEM — and it is ALREADY IN THIS LIBRARY, newly load-bearing

**[`the-rush-cost-budget-gate`](the-rush-cost-budget-gate.md) — confused (BC2020)'s "rush
cost".** *"we implemented a rush cost: if it's still before round 250 and the rush isn't
over"* … *"then everything non-rush gets an additional rush cost of 250. This meant that we
would always prioritize offense over defense."*

**Why this is the recommendation rather than any of the nine new files:** it is the only
mechanism in the entire corpus that turns *"defence must not slow the kill"* from a
POST-HOC BAR into a RUNTIME GATE. A virtual surcharge on non-offensive spending, live only
while the raid is live, makes a defensive build **self-limiting by arithmetic** — it gets
bought exactly when it is worth more than the surcharge, and never otherwise.

**⚠ Its `WHAT WOULD KILL IT` section was written under `PLAY_DEFENCE: never` and needs
re-reading, not re-writing.** It correctly warns that confused's premise was *"in a battle
of rush vs. rush"* and that a unilateral drawdown against a passive defender is a donation.
**Under the amended programme that caveat becomes the design: the surcharge is the thing
that lets us admit defence at all, because it bounds it.**

**BUILDER HOOK, unchanged from that file and still the smallest version:** one store slot
`SLOT_STRIKE_ALIVE`, one constant `NON_STRIKE_SURCHARGE`, applied in the existing
affordability check while `get_current_round() < 250` and the slot is non-zero. Zero new
units, zero new entity types, no scale delta. **Score it on median kill round AND game
share AND core-death rate, on unrated legs against live teams — never on `bots/*_probe`.**

|---|---|

| quoted spans in the 10 new files | **98** |

**Negative controls, verbatim, all returning 0 across the whole corpus:**
`quernstone flibbertigibbet` · `defense towers were no longer necessary to my strategy so
I removed them` (real: *"so I disabled them"*) · `the version with 47 lost 90% of the
matches` (real: *"of the games"*) · `static defense has to pay for itself with a
countervailing advantage in economy` (real sentence continues differently) · `falling back
to defend HQs wasted too much time` (real: *"far too much time"*) · `we measured that our
defense did not slow our attack` · `median kill round` · `our defence did not delay the
win`.

### THE NINE NEAR-MISSES, all found by an end-to-end re-grep of this sweep's own draft

**This is the library's recurring failure arriving in my own text, and the mechanical audit
caught every instance.**

* **1 WRONG-FILE ATTRIBUTION.** *"that enabled me to AB test two bots on every single map I
  had at my disposal"* was drafted against **confused (BC2025)** because the passage is in
  the first person singular. The literal grep puts it in **Just Woke Up** — a two-author
  postmortem with a first-person Automations section. **Verbatim caught what
  verbatim-plus-plausibility would have waved through.**
* **4 PARAPHRASES SITTING INSIDE QUOTATION MARKS**, all my own compressions used as labels:
  `"So much fuel they could no longer attack"` (real: *"using so much fuel to be produced
  that they could no longer attack"*), `"Fed into enemy lines"` (real: *"either being fed
  into enemy lines"*), `"Attacks focused on bugs in the defense code"` (real: *"most high
  GCL attacks are focused on bugs in the defense code"*), `"Stalling global production"`
  (recased from lowercase). All four replaced with the source strings.
* **3 QUOTE-CHARACTER MISMATCHES** — straight apostrophes typed where the sources carry
  curly (`can’t`, `don’t`, `wasn’t`, `bot’s`). Same class as sweep 22's correction.
* **1 INVISIBLE CHARACTER** — Just Woke Up's unit list carries a **zero-width space** after
  the bullet glyph in *"Defense Tower ○​ Shoots enemies to earn money"*, so the span as
  drafted could never match. Re-quoted as two separate spans.

### AND A CORRECTION TO THE EXISTING LIBRARY

**[`2026-08-09-sweep-1.md`](2026-08-09-sweep-1.md) §3** renders BC2019 smite as
`"defensive units to be overproduced… wasting resources and stalling global production"`.
**The source reads *"defensive units would be overproduced"*.** Inside quotation marks that
is a paraphrase — small, and exactly the class the INDEX's method block exists to catch.

### TWO NEW METHOD TRAPS FOR THE INDEX

1. **A ZERO-WIDTH SPACE defeats the literal grep and is invisible in every terminal.**
   Google-Docs-exported PDFs carry them around bullet glyphs. **Symptom: a quote you can
   SEE on screen returning "not found".** Fix: quote a substring that avoids the glyph.
2. **PAGE FURNITURE INJECTED MID-SENTENCE, which the `\f` fix does not cover** — this
   sweep hit it twice: *"having our starting 14 tower have a chance of not dying"* and
   *"if there were still 8 Figure 10: Tower marks enemy units around"*. Fix: quote the two
   halves as separate spans and say so, never silently splice.

## GAPS AND WHAT THIS SWEEP DID NOT DO

* **No corpus cut was run.** Every "our numbers" statement in these files is cited from
  existing repo documents (s30's 433/1024 and 399/1024; median kill 174 / median death 187
  / 46.3%; the crash census). **None was re-derived here** and the sweep was not briefed to.
* **Publication bias is the honest limit on arm B.** These are narrative postmortems. The
  finding is *"nobody REPORTS a time-to-win number"*, not *"nobody computed one"* — though
  the consequence is identical, since an unreported method cannot be ported.
* **Halite, Lux and Terminal score at a fixed horizon**, so "time to win" is not a quantity
  that exists in them. **The negative is strongest exactly where it matters most:
  Battlecode's game ends on a killed HQ and its 24 documents contain zero of all 27 terms.**
* `forum.c1games.com` returned nothing to `curl` (bot wall), so Terminal community threads
  are unread; the Terminal material here is one team's README plus the starter kit.
